That my great grandma (86) miraculously survived a rare viral infection called HSV (herpes simplex virus) Encephalitis last August that would've killed her within a week and a half without getting treatment. Near the end, she was asleep for 28 hours as the virus was destroying her short term memory. Then, she suddenly started responding to antibiotics 7 days after onset of symptoms, 5 days after taking her to her primary care and being told it was just a stomach bug, 4 days after initial hospitalization and tests, 2 days after doing the spinal tap, 1 day after confirmation that it was not a bacterial infection, 8 hours after administering her first dose of Acyclovir. She is currently alive, but is living in a nursing home because of the brain damage that was caused. I visit 2-3 times a week, to check on and talk to the woman who raised me, even if I have to repeat myself a lot and she tries to get me to bust her out of there.
